result.note: Tests the Economic Survey 2025-26's first-time citation of the Lowy Power Gap Index, its headline macro figures, and the US tariff sequence it describes.

questions.prompt: The Economic Survey 2025-26, released in January 2026, cited for the first time a Power Gap Index on which India scored -4.0, the lowest in Asia excluding Russia and North Korea. Which think tank publishes this index?
questions.explain: The Survey cited the Power Gap Index of the Australia-based Lowy Institute. A score of -4.0 indicates that India operates below its strategic potential.
questions.source: For the first time, the Survey cites Australia-based Lowy Institute’s Power Gap Index, noting that India operates below its strategic potential with a score of -4.0 – the lowest in Asia (excluding Russia and North Korea).

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey 2025-26, released in January 2026:
items: It puts India's real GDP growth estimate for FY26 at 7.4%.
It notes that the fiscal deficit came in at 4.8%, better than the 4.9% budgeted.
It notes that India received three sovereign rating downgrades.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the Survey records three sovereign rating upgrades, not downgrades. Its central paradox is that the rupee weakened despite this strong domestic performance.
questions.source: Fiscal consolidation outperformed (4.8% deficit vs 4.9% budgeted), and three sovereign rating upgrades followed.

questions.prompt: The Economic Survey 2025-26 discussed the impact of US tariffs on India in 2025. Consider the following statements:
items: An additional 25% tariff imposed in August 2025 was added on top of a 25% reciprocal duty applied from April 2025.
Later India-US negotiations led to a reduction in these tariffs.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the later negotiations did not result in a reduction. The hope that India would win a quick exemption from the new US tariff regime did not materialise.
questions.source: Instead of securing quick exemption, India was slapped with an additional 25% tariff in August – piling onto the 25% reciprocal duty from April.
